arxiv-2002-06432.title: PDDLGym : Gym Environments from PDDL Problems
arxiv-2002-06432.creator: Tom Silver, Rohan Chitnis
arxiv-2002-06432.description: Abstract We present PDDLGym , a framework that automatically constructs OpenAI Gym environments from PDDL domains and problems. Observations and actions in PDDLGym are relational, making the framework particularly well-suited for research in relational reinforcement learning and relational sequential decision-making.

arxiv-2004-06193.title: Relation Transformer Network
arxiv-2004-06193.creator: Rajat Koner, Suprosanna Shit, Volker Tresp
arxiv-2004-06193.description: Abstract The extraction of a scene graph with objects as nodes and mutual relationships as edges is the basis for a deep understanding of image content. Despite recent advances, such as message passing and joint classification, the detection of visual relationships remains a challenging task due to sub-optimal exploration of the mutual interaction among the visual objects.

arxiv-2012-10322.title: Resonant Shattering Flares as Multimessenger Probes of the Nuclear Symmetry Energy 2015 Resonant Shattering Flares as Multimessenger Probes of the Nuclear Symmetry Energy – References
arxiv-2012-10322.creator: Duncan Neill, William G. Newton, David Tsang
arxiv-2012-10322.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Duncan Neill, William G. Newton, David Tsang. The behaviour of the nuclear symmetry energy near saturation density is important for our understanding of dense nuclear matter. This density dependence can be parameterised by the nuclear symmetry energy and its derivatives evaluated at nuclear saturation density. In this work we show that the core-crust interface mode of a neutron star is sensitive to these parameters, through the (density-weighted) shear-speed within the crust, which is in turn dependent on the symmetry energy profile of dense matter.

arxiv-2303-05581.title: Open World Classification with Adaptive Negative Samples
arxiv-2303-05581.creator: Ke Bai, Guoyin Wang, Jiwei Li, Sunghyun Park, Sungjin Lee, Puyang Xu, Ricardo Henao, Lawrence Carin
arxiv-2303-05581.description: Abstract Open world classification is a task in natural language processing with key practical relevance and impact. Since the open or unknown category data only manifests in the inference phase, finding a model with a suitable decision boundary accommodating for the identification of known classes and discrimination of the open category is challenging.

arxiv-2405-07511.creator: A. A.Kilin, E. N.Pivovarova
arxiv-2405-07511.description: Abstract This paper is concerned with the problem of an ellipsoid of revolution rolling on a horizontal plane under the assumption that there is no slipping at the point of contact and no spinning about the vertical. A reduction of the equations of motion to a fixed level set of first integrals is performed.

arxiv-2503-12590.title: Personalize Anything for Free with Diffusion Transformer
arxiv-2503-12590.creator: Haoran Feng, Zehuan Huang, Lin Li, Hairong Lv, Lu Sheng✉, Tsinghua University Beihang University Renmin University of ChinaProject page: https://fenghora.github.io/Personalize-Anything-Page/
arxiv-2503-12590.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Haoran Feng, Zehuan Huang, Lin Li, Hairong Lv, Lu Sheng✉, Tsinghua University Beihang University Renmin University of ChinaProject page: https://fenghora.github.io/Personalize-Anything-Page/. Personalized image generation aims to produce images of user-specified concepts while enabling flexible editing. Recent training-free approaches, while exhibit higher computational efficiency than training-based methods, struggle with identity preservation, applicability, and compatibility with diffusion transformers (DiTs). In this paper, we uncover the untapped potential of DiT, where simply replacing denoising tokens with those of a reference subject achieves zero-shot subject reconstruction.

arxiv-2507-11612.creator: Álvaro Ribas, Miguel Vioque, Francesco Zagaria, Cristiano Longarini, Enrique Macías, Cathie J. Clarke, Sebastián Pérez, John Carpenter, Nicolás Cuello, Itziar de Gregorio-Monsalvo
arxiv-2507-11612.description: Abstract The detection of planets in protoplanetary disks has proven to be extremely challenging. pmc-10584776.creator: Maisun Mohamed Al Zorgani, Hassan Ugail, Klaus Pors, Abdullahi Magaji Dauda
pmc-10584776.description: Glucose transporter-1 (GLUT-1) expression level is a biomarker of tumour hypoxia condition in immunohistochemistry (IHC)-stained images. However, visual assessment of GLUT-1 scores is subjective and consequently prone to inter-pathologist variability.

pmc-10598892.title: Congenital lower urinary tract obstruction with spontaneous fetal bladder rupture due to posterior urethral valves: a case report
pmc-10598892.creator: Max Adriaenssens, Veerle De Boe
pmc-10598892.description: BackgroundCongenital lower urinary tract obstruction (LUTO) is a rare but significant condition affecting fetal urinary tract development. LUTO has a range of etiologies, with posterior urethral valves (PUV) being the most common cause. The prenatal diagnosis of LUTO plays a crucial role in recognizing the condition and guiding management decisions.

pmc-11344766.title: The malonyl/acetyl-transferase from murine fatty acid synthase is a promiscuous engineering tool for editing polyketide scaffolds
pmc-11344766.creator: Lynn Buyachuihan, Simon Reiners, Yue Zhao, Martin Grininger
pmc-11344766.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Modular polyketide synthases (PKSs) play a vital role in the biosynthesis of complex natural products with pharmaceutically relevant properties. Their modular architecture makes them an attractive target for engineering to produce platform chemicals and drugs. In this study, we demonstrate that the promiscuous malonyl/acetyl-transferase domain (MAT) from murine fatty acid synthase serves as a highly versatile tool for the production of polyketide analogs.

pmc-11712686.title: Exploring Novel Molecular Targets for Alzheimer’s Disease in Neuropharmacology
pmc-11712686.creator: Shampa Ghosh, Krishna Kumar Singh, Aparajita Dasgupta Amist, Jitendra Kumar Sinha
pmc-11712686.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) remains a formidable neurodegenerative challenge, characterized by profound cognitive decline. Despite decades of research, effective disease‐modifying therapies are elusive. Recent advances in molecular neuropharmacology have unveiled potential therapeutic targets for AD, offering renewed hope.MethodThis comprehensive review explores emerging avenues to combat AD, emphasizing diverse targets with substantial promise.

pmc-13545251.title: Upcycling copper chips into Cu–Fe alloys via coating-assisted plasma sintering
pmc-13545251.creator: M R Sabour, E Taherkhani, H Rahimi, A R Khatami, G Faraji
pmc-13545251.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Upcycling metal machining waste into functional engineering materials offers a sustainable pathway for value-added manufacturing. In this work, a new coated chip plasma sintering (CCPS) strategy was introduced to produce Cu–Fe alloys from discarded copper chips. Copper chips generated by machining were first coated with Fe by arc physical vapor deposition and then consolidated through cold compaction followed by spark plasma sintering. The machining process imposed severe plastic deformation on the Cu chips, producing an ultrafine microstructure prior to consolidation.
